D.treatment: group final projects in the Lasers Course

result.effect: 85% of students described at least three instances of peer interaction

cells.quote: We found 85% of students described at least three instances of peer interaction, which reinforces the the level of agreement with POS item 9 (“. . . I actively sought advice and support”).
cells.note: The study reports a descriptive qualitative finding without a comparison condition; coding reliability was 84% agreement and Cohen’s kappa was 0.67.

cells.quote: At bivariate level, increased scores in bedtime mobile phone use were significantly correlated with decreased scores in academic performance and sleep quality.
cells.note: Cross-sectional observational association; no manipulated treatment.

O.outcome_detail: sleep quality measured by the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index

cells.quote: At bivariate level, increased scores in bedtime mobile phone use were significantly correlated with decreased scores in academic performance and sleep quality.
cells.note: The PSQI global score is coded as poorer sleep quality when higher; the study reports 85.2% above the poor-sleep threshold. Cross-sectional observational association.

O.outcome_detail: attention measured by CANTAB Rapid Visual Information Processing

cells.quote: No significant relationship between bedtime mobile phone use and cognitive functioning was reported. In particular, bedtime mobile phone use was not significantly correlated with attention and verbal memory.
cells.note: Non-significant association without an equivalence test or adequate-power claim; therefore coded ns, not 0.
